title: What's so special about Route 66?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss U.S. Route 66, the "Mother Road" from Chicago to Los Angeles. They cover its origins in the Associated Highways of America plan and advocates Cyrus Avery and John Woodruff, the 1926 designation tied to the National Highway Act, the route through eight states, roadside kitsch like the Twin Arrows, Cozy Dog Drive In, Cadillac Ranch, Meteor Crater and Roy's Cafe, the 1960 TV series Route 66, its decline after the Interstate system (I-40 completed 1984, decommissioning in 1985), Andy Payne's transcontinental foot race, and preservation efforts. The episode closes with a listener mail about fraternity hazing with music.

segments.title: Opening banter and Route 66 introduction
segments.summary: Hosts banter and introduce the topic of Route 66, noting it is the most iconic and romanticized American road.

segments.title: Roads as famous subjects in songs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how few roads are famous in pop culture and note that early roads were far more important than today.

segments.title: Origins and planning of Route 66
segments.summary: Cyrus Avery and John Woodruff advocated a Chicago to Los Angeles highway through Oklahoma rather than the Santa Fe Trail. The Associated Highways of America planned routing, numbering, signage and upkeep as car ownership grew from about 500,000 to 10 million.

segments.title: Route 66 designation and route path
segments.summary: Route 66 was designated under the National Highway Act, linking Chicago and Los Angeles through eight states and following an old Gold Rush-era wagon trail.

segments.title: Roadside attractions and kitsch
segments.summary: The hosts describe quirky roadside stops that drew travelers, including the Twin Arrows, Cozy Dog Drive In, the Giganticus Headacus, Cadillac Ranch, the Chicken Ranch reference, and Meteor Crater near Roy's Cafe.

segments.title: Route 66 TV series and its filming
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1960 TV series Route 66, its theme by Nelson Riddle, its writer's road travels, and filming across about forty states.

segments.title: Decline of Route 66 and the Interstate system
segments.summary: Postwar highway plans, the Federal Highway Act under Eisenhower, and the Interstate that replaced the route left Route 66 bypassed; it was decommissioned in 1985.

segments.title: Andy Payne's transcontinental foot race
segments.summary: Oklahoma runner Andy Payne won a transcontinental foot race from Los Angeles to New York, finishing in about 573 hours, and statues of him are along the route.

segments.title: Preservation and travel tips
segments.summary: Parts of Route 66 are on the National Register of Historic Places and the endangered highways list; special maps help travelers find the old road, and the hosts point to HowStuffWorks for more.

segments.title: Listener mail: fraternity pledge torture with music
segments.summary: A listener describes being forced to endure Lou Bega's Mambo No. 5 at full volume for hours during fraternity pledging, and the hosts ask for more stories.
